scenes.[akt2_koniec_scena].text.t: Ostromir's wagon creaks uphill towards Stone Pass, and you walk beside it without looking back. Behind you stays Wolf's Ford, with its wolves, its lies and its soup. What waits for you beyond the pass, you don't know. Ostromir swears it's nothing but good things, but then Ostromir is a merchant.

scenes.[akt3_mapa].main.doneLabel.t: Set out for Starwatch on Glass Hill

scenes.[akt3_wejscie].text.t: Beyond the pass the road frays into a path, and the path into mud. In the afternoon Głuszec crawls out from behind a hill: a dozen huts, a graveyard bigger than the village, and smoke from the tavern chimney, the only thing here that looks content. The dogs bark before they see you. People slam their shutters before they hear who you are. Friendly parts, no denying it.

scenes.[akt3a_koniec_oblawa].text.t: The manhunt hits Głuszec at dawn. You get out through the cellar and the smith's barn, and you leave behind the dogs, the shouting and the reeve, who'll swear he never laid eyes on you in his life. You crash into the forest and run for as long as your breath holds. The Imperials have your mug on paper now, so there's no point going back. That leaves Starwatch, where, they say, someone stares at the sky for a living.

scenes.[akt3a_koniec_scena].text.t: You leave Głuszec behind, with its dogs, its graveyard and Grumble's fleas. The scouts are onto your trail by now, so better not to linger. Next stop: Starwatch, where, they say, someone stares at the sky for a living.

scenes.[akt3b_mapa].main.doneLabel.t: Set out for the Camp on Crow Mountain

scenes.[akt3b_przejscie].text.t: The blade sits heavier in your hand than it looks. You come down from Starwatch at dawn, because nobody here has anything more to tell you, and the stars don't answer anyway. You know now who hired you and why. You also know that whoever does the hiring rarely stops at one job. The road east, three days of it, leads to the Camp on Crow Mountain and to a war nobody asked for. At least the blade is your own now.

scenes.[akt3b_wejscie].text.t: You trudge north for two days, and on the second, after dark, you reach the place where the forest gives way to burnt land, and the land to glass. The hills glitter, though there's no sun. On one of them stands a tower with a round dome and a shattered telescope, and from a chimney at its foot drifts smoke, as if surprised it's still there. This is the old imperial Starwatch. Someone counted the stars here, before they started falling.

scenes.[akt4_stolica_mapa].main.doneLabe.t: Go Down to the Dungeon Below the Palace

scenes.[akt4_stolica_wejscie].text.t: On the third day you see the walls. They are higher than the tales promised and more ruined than the armourers admit. At the gate there is a queue of those running away and those coming back because they had nowhere to go. The guard takes a groat from you and asks if you have anything to declare. You say no, and he winks as if he knew a better version. Ulfgród smells of smoke, tar and gutters.

scenes.[akt4_wejscie].text.t: On the third day you climb the hill the locals call Crow Mountain, because the crows haven't left since the war began. Below spreads the camp: horses, wagons, tents the colour that used to be red, and a banner nobody raises all the way up any more. Nobody stops you at the gate. The war is short of men, and the sentry sees in you two hands for work, not a suspect.

scenes.[akt4a_przejscie].text.t: The letter with the command's seal is tucked inside your shirt. You roll up your blanket, leave behind whatever business you didn't get round to, and head for the capital. The camp stays at your back, and ahead lies the road to a city where nobody likes you, but everyone seems to know who you are.

scenes.[akt4b_przejscie].text.t: The Emperor is dead, and the city doesn't know it yet. You go down the servants' stairs, pass a cook who pretends not to know you, and instead of going out into the night you turn where the cook, without looking at you, points with his chin: into the pantry, behind which another stair begins. It leads down, deeper than the palace foundations allow. The blade at your belt starts to hum quietly, and the lower you go, the louder it gets.

scenes.[akt4c_cisza_bunt].text.t: Tomasz stands at the gate with those nobody counted. Marshal Wsiewłod looks at him for a long time, then nods: the gates stay open, and whoever wants to go home gets a pass. Tomasz doesn't thank him. He knows what that pass cost.

scenes.[akt4c_cisza_jar_powrot].text.t: Thirty-two men without patches stand on the ramparts when the Incursion falls back. Wsiewłod passes them without a word, but nobody asks about a safe-conduct. It is good when fewer need hanging.

scenes.[akt4c_cisza_jar_ucieczka].text.t: Rumours come from beyond the hills of a village that suddenly has a lot of peasants, and nobody asks where from. They are in no report, which this year passes for a miracle.

scenes.[akt4c_cisza_jar_wydani].text.t: A report comes in from Gallows Hill: thirty-two, one after another. The marshal signs without reading the names. In the Camp on Crow Mountain nobody runs away in the morning now, and at night few sleep either.

scenes.[akt4c_cisza_most].text.t: The broken Bridge on the Grey delays the Jarnowians' retreat by three days. The marshal doesn't ask who broke it and enters the loss under gains.

scenes.[akt4c_cisza_pekniecie].text.t: Nobody killed the Emperor, so nobody can answer for it. The courtiers whisper of illness, of a curse, of the Blade at your belt. Marshal Wsiewłod, who doesn't believe in curses, issues a notice of natural death and has it posted on the gate. Few believe it. Everyone prefers that notice to the truth.

scenes.[akt4c_cisza_ranni].text.t: The healer Dobromiła sends wagons of wounded into the city, imperial and Jarnowian under one roof. The marshal watches them being brought in and for the first time that day gives no order.

scenes.[akt4c_cisza_studnia].text.t: Nobody drinks from the well outside Skjeldowo any more, and the Jarnowians turn their wagons back. Nobody mentions what was floating in it, either.

scenes.[akt4c_cisza_wsiewlod].text.t: By morning Marshal Wsiewłod has the palace, the city and the army, in that order. He speaks briefly, without ceremony: the war goes on, orders stand, whoever has had enough will get bread and a paper, but not today. An army that didn't know that night whether it still had an Emperor remembers that it has an enemy. The Incursion falls back from the first hill, then from the second, at the cost of men who will never tire again. The city gets a commandant. Below the Palace, what held him up has been switched off.

scenes.[akt4c_cisza_wstep].text.t: When you come out of the dungeon, the palace is different. Nobody gives orders any more, but nobody knows yet what to do with the silence. On the stairs sit the cook and a footman, both without trays, staring at the wall like men after a funeral where it isn't proper to weep.

scenes.[akt4c_cisza_wywiad_falsz].text.t: Forty Jarnowians at the fort on the Old Road become the greatest victory of this war. In the city they already speak of three hundred. The command takes the credit and writes of its shrewdness.

scenes.[akt4c_cisza_wywiad_prawda].text.t: The burned wagon train at the crossing goes into the report as a coincidence. The marshal has the two carters who survived hanged and keeps looking. Nobody asks about the ninety groats.

scenes.[akt4c_cisza_wywiad_proch].text.t: On the Grey the Jarnowians lost the ford to a single volley that misfired. The marshal counts it a merit of the imperial spirit, and the quartermaster on the far bank doesn't sit down for a month.

scenes.[akt4c_cisza_zamach].text.t: The old soldier from the Last Watchtower sits on the palace steps with a knife on his knees. Nobody arrests him. He hands the knife to the marshal himself, hilt first. "For those who weren't counted," he says once more, quietly, and goes back to his own.

scenes.[akt4c_dlug_wstep].text.t: Towards morning, when the noise of the city dies down, you go down once more to the empty chamber of the Core. The light of the copper cables fades out completely. Where the Steward stood, there is someone you haven't seen since the night you woke with your wounds closed: the Being with the black glass face, in which stars shine. The cables under its feet shrink like snakes before a fire. For the first time it gives no command. For the first time it waits for you to say something.

scenes.[akt4c_przejscie].text.t: Marshal Wsiewłod signs the pass without raising his head from the map. "A man without colours. Someone on that island has to talk to them in the end, and I have nobody who wouldn't shoot." He seals it with wax and hands it to you like a bill for something you've already eaten. A boat waits in the harbour, with no name, no pennant and no questions. It sails to Jarnowo Harbour, three days from here, to the island of the smiths.

scenes.[akt5_wejscie].text.t: On the third day you see the Shipyard chimney, then the skeleton of a boat sticking out of the slipway like a ribcage. Jarnowo Harbour smells of tar, salt and burnt timber, and the sentry at the jetty studies your pass for longer than reading it takes. He doesn't hang you. The war's running short on rope.

scenes.[akt5a_przejscie].text.t: From the approach to Bald Rock, steps cut in black glass lead upward. The hetman's boat waits at the foot, and the helmsman stares at the ground. "From here on you're on your own," he says again. You climb. There are no tracks on the steps, only a thin mist and a low rumble, as if someone upstairs were shifting heavy furniture.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_bogdana].text.t: Bogdan's work holds up. Not a single nick.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_c].text.t: Three weeks later you're sitting in a roadside inn whose name you didn't catch, over a bowl of soup you didn't order. Nobody asks your name. Every now and then, without thinking about it, you glance at the sky. It's deep blue, no scars, no light in the crack. You tell yourself it's none of your business, and you almost believe it.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_cesarz_bunt].text.t: The Emperor comes up in the inns less and less. Those who remember the night the gates were opened don't tell it out loud.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_cesarz_pekniecie].te.t: The Emperor comes up in the inns less and less. The notice of natural death still hangs on the gate. But you know better.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_cesarz_zamach].text.t: The Emperor comes up in the inns less and less. Those who remember the knife in the chamber speak of him like a bill that somebody finally settled.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_dlug].text.t: The debt is paid. Now and then you check whether it's only a word, but nothing weighs on you, and that's probably the answer.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_list_astrolog].text.t: Hieronim writes at length and illegibly about what else he managed to read from the shards. Brygida adds one line in the margin: "Don't read his letters in one go, or you won't finish by spring."

scenes.[akt6_epilog_list_smyk].text.t: Nipper sends a scrap of paper with one sentence written left-handed: "They shut the palace, but I know other doors." Underneath he's drawn a snail. You don't know why.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_list_straznik].text.t: The old soldier from the Last Watchtower sends a three-word message: "Watchtower stands. Return." You read it for longer than you need to.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_list_tomasz].text.t: Tomasz writes from the ravine that people are going back to their homes, and that he himself isn't yet. He adds that he hopes you don't hold it against him that he writes so seldom.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_list_wedrowcy].text.t: A letter comes from Głuszec, signed by several hands. The inn has a new roof, and by the fire there's still a bench waiting for somebody with your name.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_most].text.t: The broken Bridge on the Grey was rebuilt from the planks of wrecked boats, and the carters say it creaks differently from the old one.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_ostrze_p].text.t: The weapon of star metal is stuck in a chopping block by the inn door, so that whoever splits the firewood has something to split it with. Nobody guesses it has seen more than the forest.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_ostrze_w].text.t: The weapon of star metal hangs over the inn's hearth, because the innkeeper insisted and you didn't have the strength to argue. When someone asks what it is, you say it's a family keepsake.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_ostrze_z].text.t: You gave the weapon of star metal to a smith for horseshoes, reckoning that the last thing it can do is something useful for horses.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_ostrze_zb].text.t: You gave the weapon of star metal to Bogdan for horseshoes. The smith held it up to the light, nodded, and said it was a shame, but horses don't ask about pedigree.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_prawda].text.t: Sometimes you remember what she said at the end: that she was no better than the Emperor, only more tired. You don't know if that was true or one last bargain. You tell yourself it makes no difference, and three days later you're thinking about it again.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_ranni].text.t: Dobromiła is still stitching up Jarnowians and Imperials under one roof, and nobody asks about uniforms any more.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_s].text.t: Three weeks later you're sitting in a roadside inn whose name you didn't catch, over a bowl of soup you didn't order. Nobody asks your name. At the next table two carters argue over which of them has the worse horses. You don't reach for your belt any more. No point.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_studnia].text.t: The well outside Skjeldowo stayed poisoned, and people in the area talk about it in whispers.

scenes.[akt6_epilog_szklo].text.t: Sometimes you remember the glass from the crater. You took it yourself; nobody told you to. You can't blame anyone else for that either.

scenes.[akt6_koniec_cisza_po_wirze].text.t:
QUIET AFTER THE WHIRL

A roadside inn, a bowl of soup, now and then a glance at the sky. "Something frighten you, sir?" the innkeeper asks. "No," you say. "Just checking it's still there." It is. For now.

scenes.[akt6_koniec_swiety_spokoj].text.t:
PEACE AND QUIET

A roadside inn, a bowl of soup, nobody asks your name. "Yes, it's me, the one from that brawl," you say when someone finally does. "Oh, you're the soup man?" says the innkeeper, and pours.

scenes.[akt6_pods_uciekla].text.t: You left the door someone walked out through, and you don't know whether it closed behind them for good. The question stays open, like a lot of questions after a war.

scenes.[akt6_pods_zginela].text.t: You closed a door that somebody had left open, and nobody will go through it now. Whether you did right, you don't know. But nobody will open that door again, and you can sleep with that.

scenes.[akt6_podsumowanie].text.t: You've wriggled out of somebody else's business that you never chose. What's left is letters, a debt that's gone, and a bowl of soup that goes cold faster than you can eat it. Today there's nothing you have to do, and that's all you wanted.

scenes.[akt6_wojna_hetman_b].text.t: Hetman Skjeldomir lays down his arms without ceremony, in his tent, with the lamp out. Nobody learns what talked him into it, and he won't tell anyone. The war ends the way it began: on somebody's orders that nobody remembers.

scenes.[akt6_wojna_hetman_p].text.t: Hetman Skjeldomir ends the war in public, on the quay, in front of his men. He says it was somebody else's idea, and that he understood it from the glass recording he heard in the tent: late, but not too late to say so. He hands out the lead soldiers from his map to the harbour children, one each, as a joke or a keepsake.

scenes.[akt6_wojna_kuznia_b].text.t: Every tenth handgun from Ragnar's forge burst in the shooter's hands, and the Hetman took it for a sign. Nobody found out it was just the workmanship.

scenes.[akt6_wojna_kuznia_s].text.t: The Islanders' Forges stand silent, the hammers still. The last handguns never left the workshop, and Ragnar now hammers out horseshoes and doesn't complain.

scenes.[akt6_wojna_proch_k].text.t: The harbour arsenal hands over its last barrels without enthusiasm and without questions. The powder goes up in the final volleys over the bay, and the war ends with a bang nobody wanted to hear any more.

scenes.[akt6_wojna_proch_u].text.t: Somewhere in the dunes lie four barrels that only the skipper and you know about. Nobody is looking for them. For now.

scenes.[akt6_wojna_proch_z].text.t: The arsenal is short of powder for the last volleys, so the last shots are sparing and far between. The skipper says the barrels are on the bottom by the Boat Graveyard, and that the fish are cheerful about it.

scenes.[akt6_wojna_wiesc].text.t: The letter from the mainland that you gave the Hetman lay on his table to the end. They say he read it more than once.

scenes.[akt6_wojna_wstep].text.t: The handguns fall silent one by one, like dogs when the wind turns. Word reaches the harbour that the Being has stopped feeding the war, and that without her, powder and steel have no addressee. Nothing on the island sounds like a victory.

scenes.[demo_kram_wstep].text.t: The quartermaster sits behind a counter of rough planks, counting bandages. "What, eyes popped out of your skulls? Buy something, don't gawk. Gawking never put a groat in anybody's purse!" He grumbles that in his day a pupil tore up his own rags for bandages.

scenes.[demo_kurier].text.t: Wolf's Ford Watchtower is a palisade, a tower and mud up to your ankles. The sentry takes his sweet time before he opens the gate to a half-dead wanderer in a crumpled tunic in the school's colours, caked in mud to the knees. Commander Wszebor looks you up and down and tells you to come inside. The tribute party's insignia lie at the bottom of your bundle; nobody has asked yet, and you don't mean to answer.

scenes.[demo_mapa].main.doneLabel.t: Set out for Głuszec, beyond Stone Pass

scenes.[demo_sparing].text.t: Gnieworad shoves a wooden club into your fist and pushes you out into the middle of the yard. "You hold that like an old woman holds a broom. Radogost, show these slugs how we make men out of them!" The drillmaster cracks his knuckles, and the other pupils guffaw.

scenes.[demo_sparing_porazka].text.t: You lie in the mud seeing stars, though it's the middle of the day. "Up," Radogost snaps, "this isn't your feather bed!" The pupils bray so loud the crows scatter.

scenes.[demo_sparing_wygrana].text.t: Radogost clutches his ribs and turns the air blue. "Devil take you, lad, you hit like a smith on an anvil!" Gnieworad says nothing, just nods, and that's a rare thing with him.

scenes.[demo_swit].text.t: Fog hangs over the drill yard, thick as cream, and the kitchen smells of smoke and burnt onion. Master Gnieworad stands in the gate, glowering as if every one of you owed him undying gratitude for the daily shouting, the lessons that lead nowhere and the back-breaking drill. "You lot, you slugs! Give me your names. I'm not bawling 'hey, you' over your graves!"

scenes.[prolog_kurier_narracja].text.t: Around noon a horse in a lather bursts into the yard, and on it a man in a red cloak, the like of which the village hasn't seen since the last levy. The pupils freeze, wooden clubs in their fists. Gnieworad walks out of the gate slowly, with the face of a man who already knows what he's about to hear.

scenes.[prolog_wstep].text.t: The Empire runs from the salt sea to mountains nobody has crossed yet, and inside its borders there is one rule: pay your tax, keep your head down, don't talk about the stars. The old folk say the night sky used to be quieter. Now every few years something flares up there and comes down beyond the forest, and after the spark storms and the strange fogs there are fewer people in the villages. Imperial scribes enter it in their books as natural disasters, and that settles it. The peasants spit over their left shoulder, throw another log on the fire and pretend they saw nothing.

scenes.[prolog_wstep_wies].text.t: Birchgrove is the last village before the Foothills, a godforsaken place so far from the capital that folk here know the Emperor only from his coin, and the tax collector all too well. On its edge, for centuries now, has stood the School of the Blade, where they make warriors out of paupers, and out of warriors, meat for whoever pays. Whoever ends up here gets a choice of sword or spear, barley porridge without a lick of fat, and Master Gnieworad, who reminds you every morning that nothing here is free, not even a smack in your stupid mug. Today is an ordinary day. Or so it looks in the morning.

scenes.[prolog_wymarsz].text.t: At dawn the next day Gnieworad doesn't say goodbye, he just counts heads. Four. "Four names, four heads, the courier will be pleased," he mutters, without so much as a look at you. Only at the gate does he add: "And quit shaking in your breeches. The wraith's not as black as he's painted. Mind, the ones who paint him never saw him, because the ones who saw him don't paint anything any more." The courier has left you a guide, a close-mouthed man from the Foothills. Wolf's Ford is two days' march, and from there it's on to the capital. You sling your bundles and walk out of the gate before the master thinks up something worse.

scenes.[schody_1_po].text.t: The hoods drop onto the steps, empty. The blade hums louder. The stairs go on, and nobody ever fitted a handrail here.

scenes.[schody_1_porazka].text.t: You wake a few steps lower, face on the stone and everything aching. The hoods stand over you, but they no longer come near. They watch you get up and go on down. They are not guarding against anyone coming in. They are guarding against anyone leaving.

scenes.[schody_1_wstep].text.t: After forty steps the palace ends. Brick gives way to stone that nobody ever dressed. On the landing stand two hooded figures, pale as flour, skin right down to the bone. They don't breathe, but they watch. An officer would say: a guard. The Emperor has been dead an hour, and nobody has told them.

scenes.[schody_2_po].text.t: Rags and cold are left on the steps. The tally marks on the wall end in the middle of a five. You don't count how many more. The stairs don't count either.

scenes.[schody_2_porazka].text.t: You wake a few steps lower, face on the stone and everything aching. The hoods stand over you, but they no longer come near. They watch you get up and go on down. They are not guarding against anyone coming in. They are guarding against anyone leaving.

scenes.[schody_2_wstep].text.t: The stairs wind into a spiral so tight you walk sideways. On the walls there are notches, tally marks counted in fives, thousands of them. Someone counted the tribute here, and then someone counted those who carried it. Three hoods come down from under the vault, one after another, as if coming back from dinner.

scenes.[schody_3_po].text.t: The last hood sinks down without a sound. Behind it the stairs end and something begins that has walls, doors and a noise of its own. Somewhere far off, something big is working. There is no way back anyway.

scenes.[schody_3_porazka].text.t: You wake a few steps lower, face on the stone and everything aching. The hoods stand over you, but they no longer come near. They watch you get up and go on down. They are not guarding against anyone coming in. They are guarding against anyone leaving.

scenes.[schody_3_wstep].text.t: The air here is warm as from an oven and smells of iron. The blade hums so that you feel it in your teeth. On the last landing stand two hoods, bigger than the others, and behind them a corridor is visible. Beyond that nobody sweeps any more, and it shows there has been no reason to for a long time.
